topic: Hoover Dam's hidden fridge: concrete cooled by 582 miles of pipe

lines.say: A hundred and twenty-five years. That's how long Hoover Dam would take to cool in one pour.
Setting cement makes heat. The hot core fights the cooling skin, and it cracks.
So it went up in separate columns.
Inside each, coils of one-inch steel pipe. Over five hundred eighty miles.
River water first, then ice water from a giant refrigeration plant.
As heat drains, the columns shrink apart.
Grout fills the gaps and pipes, making one solid dam.
Cooled in under two years, not a century.
Follow for how the world is really engineered.
